input.hypothesis: The Strait of Hormuz closes to commercial tanker traffic

nodes.statement: The Strait of Hormuz closes to commercial tanker traffic
nodes.resolution: Lloyd's List reports a closure lasting more than 48 hours
nodes.rationale: A closure disrupts roughly a fifth of seaborne oil flows before buyers can reroute.
assumptions: Naval deterrence does not prevent an initial closure
nodes.marketQuery: Strait of Hormuz closure tanker traffic 2026

nodes.statement: War-risk insurance for Gulf transits doubles
nodes.resolution: Quoted war-risk premium exceeds 2% of hull value
nodes.rationale: Underwriters reprice quickly when vessels cannot assess the security of a transit.
assumptions: Insurers continue writing cover rather than withdrawing entirely
nodes.marketQuery: Gulf war risk insurance premium tanker

nodes.statement: OPEC+ announces an emergency spare-capacity release
nodes.resolution: A ministerial statement names additional barrels available within 30 days
nodes.rationale: Producer governments have a strong incentive to limit a price shock but physical delivery is constrained.
assumptions: Saudi spare capacity can reach export terminals

nodes.statement: A credible naval escort arrangement restores escorted tanker transits
nodes.resolution: Major insurers accept escorted passages through the strait
nodes.rationale: A negotiated escort channel can reduce the effective supply outage before a full diplomatic settlement.
assumptions: Escorts are acceptable to coastal states

nodes.statement: Asian refiners bid for replacement barrels outside the Gulf
nodes.resolution: Spot differentials for Atlantic Basin crude widen for five trading days
nodes.rationale: Refiners can switch marginal barrels, but freight and grade constraints make the response expensive.
assumptions: Atlantic Basin exporters have prompt cargo availability
nodes.marketQuery: Asian refiners replacement crude spot differentials

nodes.statement: Brent settles above 100 dollars per barrel within the horizon
nodes.resolution: ICE Brent front-month settlement exceeds 100 dollars
nodes.rationale: The option-like threshold concentrates the market consequence of the supply interruption.
assumptions: Demand destruction remains limited during the first month

nodes.name: Brent crude
nodes.rationale: Front-month Brent is the liquid benchmark for the immediate physical supply shock.
assumptions: The futures curve remains a usable signal of prompt scarcity

nodes.name: US Global Jets ETF
nodes.rationale: Airline margins respond negatively to jet-fuel costs before fares can reset.
assumptions: Fuel hedges do not fully offset a rapid crude move

edges.mechanism: A closure forces underwriters to reprice a transit
assumptions: Reported incidents are sufficient for an actuarial response

edges.mechanism: The disruption creates political pressure for a supply response
A closure makes an escorted corridor politically urgent
Lost Gulf barrels force refiners to seek substitute cargoes
Interrupted seaborne supply reprices prompt crude
assumptions: The disruption removes at least several million barrels per day

edges.mechanism: Higher freight and insurance costs raise landed crude prices
Additional prompt barrels cap the price spike
Competition for replacement cargoes widens spot differentials
The benchmark reaches the threshold price
Restored escorted transits reduce the duration of the shock
Jet fuel costs compress airline margins

summary.headline: A Hormuz closure feeds through insurance and replacement barrels before an OPEC or escort response can cap it.
summary.mainUncertainty: Whether an escort corridor restores enough physical flow before inventories tighten.
